text: Where does code go when more than one module needs it?

text: Security rules and Keycloak calls are needed by every module that takes requests, not only by the partner module.

text: Copied into each module, every fix would have to be made twice.

text: So shared code lives in platform libraries, in one versioned platform build, next to the error and OTP libraries.

text: The security library secures any app: access tokens, realm roles, and refusals as problem details.

text: Its route rules are configuration, and anything not listed is refused.

text: It configures itself before Spring Boot's own defaults, and an app can still replace it.

text: A module adds its own filter to that one chain through a customizer, and a customizer that sets route rules stops startup.

text: The Keycloak library is a small admin client that logs in as its own client and refreshes its token.

text: Every call has a configured timeout, a refused token is replaced once, and each failure is a problem detail: conflict, rejected, or unavailable.
